edits.old: ## 5. Preserve the verified F2W baseline before importing donor behavior
edits.new:
### 4.13 Tiled sign-in and admin-only capabilities

Tiled is the identity and admin-role authority for each environment. F2W validates credentials and resolves the actual user principal/admin status against the configured local, staging or production instance, not an endpoint supplied in an LLM argument. Authentication and the technical admin writer are separate: never use the service writer's identity to decide whether an end user is an admin. Map verified non-admin users to chat-only access and verified admins to ingestion, curation, approval, scoped graph editing and publication. Ordinary chat can use bounded read-only Tools and maintain its own session/preferences; it cannot automatically trigger enrichment or corpus writes when evidence is weak.

No separate named maintainer allowlist or assumed OAuth2-proxy is introduced. The exact native Tiled login/session integration is verified at H1; do not invent an auth endpoint or infer admin from an email, HTTP header or client boolean. Test login/logout, expiry/revocation, cross-environment token rejection and admin downgrade. Local mode must support a narrow authenticated login path without exposing a general admin GraphQL proxy. Existing frontend endpoints/DTOs/SSE remain compatible for authorized use; minimal login/capability presentation is an explicit owner-directed addition.

ApprovalRecord stores verified approving principal, target Tiled instance, role-check timestamp, scope, snapshot/plan hash and decision. Recheck authority before privileged effects; persistent approved job grants must be bounded and cannot survive account revocation as unchecked global authority. A headless worker executes an authenticated administrator's authorized job; background service possession of the admin key is not a substitute for authorization. The same policy applies through direct Python, FastAPI, Tools, workers and FORGE delegation.

### 4.14 Git is the versioned JSON promotion channel

Frozen versioned JSON KGs and their manifests are committed to the F2W repository on the reviewed integration path. Proposed layout is storage/kg/<corpus>/<snapshot-id>/graph.json and manifest.json; preserve existing selectable paths via compatibility references where needed. Commit-ready artifacts contain derived graph facts, permitted relevant excerpts and stable private evidence references, not PDFs, source-paper dumps, figure crops, credentials, local paths or operational databases. If a current JSON contains source material that must stay private, stop and separate private payloads through explicit references before committing; do not silently drop facts or claim a public repo is an access-control boundary.

Promotion selects an immutable Git commit, repository-relative path and SHA-256. Staging validates those exact bytes and records the required binary report against that hash. Production receives the same committed JSON and manifest onto its mounted storage and verifies hashes and compatible schema/importer before a production-specific approved import. No extraction, parsing, model calls, identity re-resolution or schema reinterpretation occurs to transfer a tested KG. Missing private evidence dependencies are copied/mounted through their separately authorized channel and verified; they are not rebuilt invisibly and never added to Git merely to make promotion pass.

Code image digest, data commit/snapshot hash and target import receipt are distinct identifiers. Committing a graph does not bake it into an image or authorize publication. Docker build contexts/layers must continue excluding storage/kg corpus artifacts even when tracked by Git. The deployment/release process exports only the reviewed data files from the selected commit into runtime mounts. Staging receipts cannot authorize production. Record the commit after it exists in an external release/promotion record; do not make a manifest claim its own containing commit hash. An admin edit is journaled, reconciled into a new JSON version, tested and committed before cross-environment promotion.

### 4.15 Confirmed central infrastructure and separate repository governance

The owner confirms tiled-staging.als.lbl.gov and tiled.als.lbl.gov run Tiled Graph 0.2.19 and acknowledges coordination around admin publication. Treat the old failed public release lookups as historical drafting limitations, not evidence against this confirmation. The implementing/deploying team still records the actual build/image digest, target identity and issued environment-specific secret references and executes authorized connection/role/edit checks. No operator contact, account name or secret is invented by this plan.

F2W work remains on forge_merge with owner-controlled H0-H7. FORGE integration is prepared in a separate reviewed working copy and merged in coordination with Alex. Central deployment checks, registry publication, application rollout, Git data commits, Tiled import approval and FORGE merge remain distinct operations.

edits.old: ## 8. What can run in parallel, and what cannot
edits.new:
### T25A-T25C - Tiled authentication and role-enforced application access

T25A runs after H0 alongside T01/T18A/T24A and blocks H1. Freeze the actual native Tiled sign-in/admin-resolution contract, environment binding, internal versus end-user identity, the reader/admin capability matrix and ApprovalRecord origin. Design the narrow local sign-in path and the minimal login/capability UI integration. No guessed OAuth2-proxy, allowlist, endpoint or auth header.

T25B runs after H1 in parallel with runtime T02 and blocks H2. Implement verified-principal construction, fail-closed capability checks, session boundaries and audit identity across Python/API/Tools/jobs. Use fake identity fixtures for the first UI/runtime slice; test forged admin flags, direct SDK calls, revoked grants and reader attempts to start ingestion before any effect.

T25C joins after application-owned disposable Tiled T20B. Verify real login/role/expiry/admin and regular-user flows in managed mode and connect-only mode; run every protected mutation through the shared guard with an admin writer present. It blocks H4 and the full H6 role-specific UI/FORGE demonstration. Central smoke tests remain explicitly authorized; fixture credentials never come from central production secrets.

### T26A-T26C - Git-versioned KG release and promotion

T26A runs after H0 with T23A and blocks H1: freeze the tracked JSON/manifest layout, disclosure check, data-release descriptor, artifact hashes and image exclusion. Define how schema/evidence dependencies are verified without committing source papers or secrets. Preserve existing graph payload and schema meanings.

T26B runs after H3 and JSON builder T23B, in parallel with T08B importer and domain ports. Add commit-ready artifact validation, immutable lookup/export and hash checks, a release record tied to executed binary results and evidence-availability checks. Tests use an isolated temporary Git fixture; the migration's reviewed JSON commits still integrate into forge_merge. It blocks H4's candidate-artifact acceptance.

T26C runs after H4/T13. Rehearse selecting the tested Git artifact and mounting identical bytes for a second production-profile disposable target, rejecting tampering/wrong hashes, producing a distinct target approval/receipt and doing zero inference. Demonstrate rollback by selecting an earlier committed snapshot; verify edit reconciliation creates a new committed version before cross-environment promotion. H5 reviews the exact data-release/import packet and H6 repeats package/container parity. No live production write is authorized by this rehearsal.
